key_insight: The paper makes operator learning self-explainable by decomposing predictions into localized integral contributions from different input regions, revealing which spatial patterns drive the output.
engineering_relevance: This provides physically interpretable machine learning for flow problems, helping engineers trust and diagnose predictions in blood flow and unsteady aerodynamics.
method: Reformulate operator learning as a generalized functional linear model with integral equations
Split the input domain into subdomains and compute localized integrals for regional importance
Use the built-in decomposition to explain both function-to-scalar and function-to-function mappings
evidence_signal: The framework is demonstrated on blood flow and unsteady aerodynamics cases, with results showing that high-gradient regions are most influential and qualitative agreement with post-hoc explainability methods.
watch_item: Interpretability depends on how the domain is partitioned, so subdomain design and resolution may affect the fidelity of the explanations.
paper_title: Self-explainable Operator Learning for Discovering Spatial Patterns in Functional Data
